question: A rides his bicycle at 15 km/h, while B starts his ride after 6 hours to catch A with a speed of 25 km/h. Time taken by B to catch A (in hours) is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Lead distance created by **A** = 15 × 6 = 90 km.

Relative speed (same direction) = 25 − 15 = 10 km/h.

Time taken by **B** to catch **A** = Lead Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **A** = 15 km/h

Speed of **B** = 25 km/h

Time gap = 6 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b10ee40206aa5707bf5b081aec046c03eb08e156c4f7477a99189f6968a0ee55.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by **A** in 6 hours = 15 × 6 = 90 km

⇒ When **B** starts, the distance between **A** and **B** is 90 km.

⇒ Relative speed of **B** relative to **A** = 25 − 15 = 10 km/h

⇒ Time taken by **B** to cover the gap = 90 ÷ 10

⇒ Time taken = 9 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move toward each other, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting Time Rule

The time required for a faster object to catch a slower object is given by: Meeting Time = (Initial separation distance) ÷ (Relative Speed).</p
